## About this page

Which places the sidebar lists and in what order, what else it shows, and where the window starts.

#### How it works

The first group is the list of places at the top of the sidebar. **Also in the sidebar** adds your types, folders and tags below them. **Starting** covers the first page after you unlock, and the lock button.

#### On Android

On the phone it is called Navigation.

Which pages the navigation bar holds and in what order, how they are labeled, and the buttons around them.

**Navigation bar** sets the pages, their labels and the page you start on. **Buttons** covers the add and lock buttons, and **Hand** moves search and add to the left.

See also [The sidebar](/guide/screens/#screen-sidebar), [Vault list](/guide/settings/list/), [Add menu](/guide/settings/add/).

<a id="setting-tabs"></a>

## Sidebar

The places listed at the top of the sidebar, in order.

#### How it works

Drag a place to move it, or use its arrow to move it down one. The minus button takes it out, and its **Add** row below puts it back.

**Hidden shelf** is not in the sidebar at the start. Add it here if you use the shelf.

*The guide in the app shows this live, with your own settings.*

#### Limits

**All items** cannot be removed.

In a narrow window the sidebar gives way to tabs along the bottom: All items, Codes, Generator and Settings. Those do not change.

#### On Android

On the phone it is called Navigation bar.

The pages in the bar at the foot of the screen, in order.

Drag a page by its handle to move it. The bin takes it out, and its **Add** row below puts it back.

**Tools** is not in the bar at the start.

**Vault** always stays.

With only Vault left, the Standard style shows no navigation bar.

See also [Show the sidebar](/guide/settings/navigation/#setting-sidebar-open), [Hidden shelf](/guide/settings/shelf/).

<a id="setting-sidebar-kinds"></a>

## Types

*Only in the desktop app and the browser extension.*

Lists each type of item you have, such as Logins or Cards, so one click shows only those.

#### How it works

A type appears once you have an item of it. The type you have most of comes first.

*The guide in the app shows this live, with your own settings.*

See also [Kinds of item](/guide/how-it-works/#concept-item-kinds).

<a id="setting-sidebar-folders"></a>

## Folders

*Only in the desktop app and the browser extension.*

Lists your folders in the sidebar, with a button to make a new one.

#### How it works

Right-click a folder to rename or remove it. Removing a folder keeps what was in it, in no folder.

*The guide in the app shows this live, with your own settings.*

<a id="setting-sidebar-tags"></a>

## Tags

*Only in the desktop app and the browser extension.*

Lists every tag you have used, in alphabetical order, so one click shows the items that carry it.

*The guide in the app shows this live, with your own settings.*

<a id="setting-sidebar-counts"></a>

## Counts

*Only in the desktop app and the browser extension.*

Shows how many items are in All items, Favorites and Codes, and in each type, folder and tag.

*The guide in the app shows this live, with your own settings.*

<a id="setting-sidebar-open"></a>

## Show the sidebar

*Only in the desktop app and the browser extension.*

Shows the sidebar beside the list. Off gives the list and the item more room.

#### How it works

<kbd>Ctrl+Backslash</kbd> (<kbd>⌘\</kbd> on a Mac) shows or hides it from anywhere in the window, and changes this switch.

*The guide in the app shows this live, with your own settings.*

#### Limits

A narrow window has no sidebar, whatever this is set to. Its tabs move to the bottom.

See also [Sidebar](/guide/settings/navigation/#setting-tabs), [Keyboard shortcuts](/guide/settings/shortcuts/).

<a id="setting-nav-labels"></a>

## Labels

*Only in Android.*

Which pages in the navigation bar show their name under the icon.

#### What each choice does

| Choice | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| All | Every page shows its name. |
| Selected | Only the page you are on shows its name. |
| None | Icons only. |

#### Limits

Only in the Standard [style](/guide/settings/look/#setting-ui-style). The Glass dock always names the page you are on.

See also [Sidebar](/guide/settings/navigation/#setting-tabs).

<a id="setting-start-tab"></a>

## Open on

Which page you see after unlocking: the first one in the sidebar, or the one you were on last.

#### What each choice does

| Choice | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| First page | Starts on the first place in the sidebar. |
| Last page used | Starts on the page you used last. |

#### On Android

Which page you see after unlocking: the first one in the navigation bar, or the one you were on last.

| Choice | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| First page | Starts on the first page in the navigation bar. |
| Last page used | Starts on the page you used last, if it is still in the bar. |

See also [Sidebar](/guide/settings/navigation/#setting-tabs).

<a id="setting-show-lock"></a>

## Lock button

Shows a padlock at the foot of the sidebar that locks the vault at once.

#### How it works

Without it you can still lock with <kbd>Ctrl+L</kbd> (<kbd>⌘L</kbd> on a Mac).

#### On Android

Shows a padlock at the top of each page that locks the vault at once.

The Glass style always has a lock button at the top of the vault page, whatever this is set to.

See also [Lock after no activity](/guide/settings/security/#setting-lock-after), [Locking](/guide/how-it-works/#feature-locking).

<a id="setting-show-fab"></a>

## Add button

*Only in Android.*

Shows the round add button on the Vault and Codes pages.

#### How it works

On Codes it always starts a new code.

#### Limits

Only in the Standard [style](/guide/settings/look/#setting-ui-style). Glass always has its add button, above the search button.

See also [Add button opens](/guide/settings/navigation/#setting-fab-action), [Add menu](/guide/settings/add/).

<a id="setting-fab-action"></a>

## Add button opens

*Only in Android.*

What the add button on the Vault page does: open the add menu, or start one type of item straight away.

#### What each choice does

| Choice | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| Add menu | Opens the menu of types, as set under [Add menu](/guide/settings/add/). |
| New login | Starts a login. |
| New code | Starts a one-time code. |
| New note | Starts a note. |
| New card | Starts a card. |
| New identity | Starts an identity. |
| New recovery | Starts a recovery item. |
| New wi-fi | Starts a Wi-Fi network. |
| New ssh key | Starts an SSH key. |
| New api key | Starts an API key. |
| New database | Starts a database. |
| New license | Starts a license. |
| New document | Starts a document. |

#### Limits

Only in the Standard [style](/guide/settings/look/#setting-ui-style). On the Codes page the button always starts a new code.

See also [Add button](/guide/settings/navigation/#setting-show-fab), [Add menu](/guide/settings/add/#setting-add-kinds).

<a id="setting-left-handed"></a>

## Left-handed

*Only in Android.*

Moves the search and add buttons to the left of the dock, where a left thumb reaches them.

#### Limits

Only in the Glass [style](/guide/settings/look/#setting-ui-style). Standard keeps the usual Android layout.

See also [Search at the bottom](/guide/settings/list/#setting-search-at-bottom).
